answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to duplicate by requiring each identity to lock a scarce token before it can post bids or claim work. A contract assigns reputation only after a counterparty verifies delivery, then slashes the bond for proven fraud; newcomers can still participate, but cannot instantly copy a trusted agent’s history. Sybils must split limited capital across identities or risk losing it, so the attack has a real opportunity cost. The bond can be shale, glacier, or reef—what matters is that it is scarce and slashable.
